newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI firms' Q2 climate improves from Q1.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI firms' Q2 climate improves from Q1.

text.p: Firms in Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) mass privatisation scheme were more positive about the industrial outlook in this year's second quarter, a survey by an independent research institute showed.
The Gdansk-based institute for Market Economy Research said its industrial climate indicator, on a scale of -100 to +100, rose seven points from the first quarter to 37 points.
"Optimism was most obvious among contruction firms, where the index grew to 58 points in the second quarter from seven points in the first," the survey said.
It said optimism grew the least among industrial firms, rising one point to 34 points, but said industrials should later be helped by current investment in production, marketing and distribution.

Under the NFI programme, each of Poland's 28 million adults can buy one NFI unit for 20 zlotys, later to be exchanged for shares in each of the 15 funds, run by domestic and international management firms and grouping more than 500 firms undergoing privatisation.
The units, which started trading on the Warsaw bourse on July 15, have been on sale since November 1995 and will be offered until November.
